summary: Poland supports onshore renewables through 15-year Contracts for Difference paid by a state-owned settlement company, and offshore wind through 25-year support under the 2020 Offshore Wind Act. Renewables produced more electricity than lignite in 2024, and profits can be repatriated freely.

access.reason: Onshore projects win support in auctions, and offshore wind has its own auctions planned for 2025 and 2027.

terms.reason: Auction winners get a 15-year contract for difference against a fixed price, and offshore wind gets up to 25 years of support.

buyer.reason: Support is paid by Zarządca Rozliczeń, a state-owned settlement company.

ownership.reason: The zloty is fully convertible, and profits can be repatriated.

stability.reason: The Energy Policy until 2040 plans offshore wind growth, and green certificates are being phased out in favour of auctions.

direction.reason: Renewables overtook lignite in 2024, led by solar and wind growth.

ownership.reason: The zloty is fully convertible, and profits can be repatriated.

direction.reason: No change for C&I buyers was found in the sources reviewed.
